claims.text: A machine-learning potential should be developed using ab initio data for high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning potential will improve representation of the atomic configurations sampled by the ab initio liquid.
Improved representation of liquid configurations will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys at and near their melting temperatures.
The applicable composition range comprises alloys with three to six principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is 0.8 to 1.2 times the alloy melting temperature.
Short-range and medium-range order in the liquid are the structural mediators of the proposed improvement.
Improved potential functions permit molecular-dynamics simulations to represent the complex atomic configurations of high-entropy alloys more accurately.
The machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will yield more accurate free-energy calculations.
The accuracy of the machine-learning potential may depend on the quality and quantity of its ab initio training data.
The potential may have limited transferability across composition and temperature ranges.
The hypothesis is falsified if thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is reduced by less than 20% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
